rationale: The most clinically common FGA depot-to-SGA depot conversion — escaping haloperidol decanoate's EPS, tardive dyskinesia risk, hyperprolactinaemia and QTc burden while maintaining the adherence benefits of depot administration. Paliperidone palmitate's two-dose deltoid loading protocol (150 mg day 1, 100 mg day 8) reaches therapeutic levels quickly without needing a separate oral overlap. The haloperidol decanoate depot tail (half-life ~21 days; full clearance ~10 weeks) provides ongoing D2 cover during the PP-LAI loading period — combined exposure is clinically acceptable and preferred over a bare switch. Skip the next scheduled decanoate injection and commence PP-LAI loading. Monitor QTc: haloperidol's high QTc contribution will diminish over weeks as the depot clears. EPS, prolactin and tardive symptoms should be reviewed at 3 months when haloperidol has substantially cleared. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Skip next Haldol decanoate injection. Give Invega Sustenna 150 mg deltoid (loading dose 1). Haloperidol depot tail continues releasing — good D2 cover maintained. Counsel patient on expected improvement in EPS over coming months.
Invega Sustenna 100 mg deltoid (loading dose 2, day 8 ± 2 days). Haloperidol depot still present. PP-LAI levels building toward therapeutic range. QTc beginning to improve as haloperidol clears.
First maintenance Sustenna injection (100 mg; deltoid or gluteal). Haloperidol decanoate substantially cleared. Assess EPS, tardive movements, prolactin. Monthly Sustenna thereafter.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: haloperidol decanoate 100 mg/4 weeks ≈ paliperidone palmitate 100 mg/4 weeks (Maudsley 15th, LAI equivalence). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
